dedupe_keys.name: predictors of evacuation behaviour route choice and web interaction dataset from virtual buildings

description: This data set records how people choose escape routes when evacuating virtual buildings, for use in calibrating evacuation simulations such as agent-based models. In an online experiment, participants completed a random subset of evacuation tasks in which they reached T-intersections whose layout parameters were controlled, and chose a corridor by clicking; the data capture decision time, mouse rotation, the chosen corridor and self-rated confidence, plus demographic information and answers to closing questionnaires. The producers are Dajana Snopková, Martin Tancoš, Lukáš Herman and Vojtěch Juřík, who describe it in Scientific Data (2025). Coverage is 208 respondents aged 17 to 71 after exclusion of those with serious technical problems. The data are free on figshare under CC BY as CSV files in a 10 MB archive; the descriptor article is open access under CC BY-NC-ND, and the authors state the data may be used by academic and commercial users. Caveats: participants took part at home on their own computers, so hardware and surroundings varied, choices were made in a virtual setting without smoke, crowds or stress, and the sample is not representative of any building population. Simulation uses: route choice parameters for building evacuation models and validation of wayfinding rules in agent-based simulations of emergencies. Related records: JuPedSim (model-jupedsim) simulates pedestrian evacuation dynamics and can use such choice parameters, and GAMA (platform-gama) hosts evacuation agent-based models.
